The guided setup assistant

Source: vignettes/guided-setup-assistant.Rmd
guided-setup-assistant.Rmd

ehr_setup_assistant() turns a set of choices into a readable R script: project configuration, download, cohort build, pipeline stages and, optionally, the analysis and merge calls. Planning is read-only. The assistant never downloads data or runs a pipeline; you review the script and run the blocks yourself, or let it write the script to a file.

sci <- ehr_setup_assistant(
  src_name = "mimic_iv_demo",
  cohort = "scid", import_scope = "hospital",
  base_dir = file.path(docs_root, "assistant-project"),
  interactive = FALSE
)
names(sci)
#> [1] "choices"    "script"     "next_steps"
sci$choices[c("src_name", "cohort", "import_scope", "engine", "db_name")]
#> $src_name
#> [1] "mimic_iv_demo"
#> 
#> $cohort
#> [1] "scid"
#> 
#> $import_scope
#> [1] "hospital"
#> 
#> $engine
#> [1] "postgres"
#> 
#> $db_name
#> [1] "rendehr"

The generated script starts with the project and the download, then shows each pipeline stage as its own block:

cat(head(sci$script, 24), sep = "\n")
#> # Generated by ehr_setup_assistant().
#> # Review this script and run it block by block in your own R session.
#> # The assistant printed this code; it did not run downloads or write to the database.
#> 
#> # Step 0 - Load rendehR --------------------------------------------------
#> # Use library(rendehR) after installation, or devtools::load_all() while developing locally.
#> library(rendehR)

#> # Every pipeline call below passes src_name explicitly.

#> # data_dir is for the large files (raw downloads, cohort parquet, DuckDB); point it at a large disk.

#> default_src <- src_names[[1]]

A harder case combines the sepsis variant, a multi-source plan, ICU-level analysis and a merge at the same grain:

sepsis <- ehr_setup_assistant(
  src_name = c("mimic_iv_demo", "eicu_demo"),
  cohort = "sepsis3", sepsis_bundle = "first_sepsis3_admission",
  import_scope = "hospital", pipeline = "full",
  analysis_level = "icu", merge = "icu",
  memory_limit = "4GB", threads = 2,
  base_dir = file.path(docs_root, "assistant-sepsis"),
  interactive = FALSE
)
sepsis$choices[c("src_names", "cohort", "sepsis_bundle", "import_scope",
                 "pipeline", "analysis_level", "merge")]
#> $src_names
#> [1] "mimic_iv_demo" "eicu_demo"    
#> 
#> $cohort
#> [1] "sepsis3"
#> 
#> $sepsis_bundle
#> [1] "first_sepsis3_admission"
#> 
#> $import_scope
#> [1] "hospital"
#> 
#> $pipeline
#> [1] "full"
#> 
#> $analysis_level
#> [1] "icu"
#> 
#> $merge
#> [1] "icu"

To keep the script, either ask for it at planning time or write the returned plan later:

plan <- ehr_setup_assistant(..., save_script = TRUE,
                            setup_script_path = "setup.R")
write_setup_script(plan, "setup.R", overwrite = TRUE)

What the assistant chooses

Cohort and scope. The cohort may be SCI, a custom ICD list, Sepsis-3 or the whole source. import_scope then decides how much context is kept: icu keeps the selected stays, hospital keeps the admission and its sibling ICU stays, patient keeps every encounter of the selected patients. SCI and custom ICD cohorts select admissions on MIMIC, so ICU scope is not offered there; sepsis selects ICU stays and accepts all three. The default for Sepsis-3 is hospital, matching build_sepsis_cohort().

Analysis level and merge. These are independent. The analysis level decides how the harmonized tables are grained; the merge decides whether the pooled schema is written at admission or ICU grain. An ICU merge builds the ICU timeline tables even when the analysis level is admission.

Engine. A DuckDB plan loads the raw data, builds the generic cohort information and runs the concept layers that DuckDB supports, then stops. To continue in PostgreSQL, generate a PostgreSQL plan and start at run_db(), reusing the cohort Parquet.

Configuration. The assistant can write missing configuration files, use an existing project, or skip configuration. It never overwrites an existing ehr_config.json or credentials file. In manual mode the script writes a comment between creating and loading the configuration, but it does not pause execution; run the generated blocks one at a time. Paths are recorded as absolute paths, and the nearest existing ancestor must be writable.

Sepsis variants in the assistant

sepsis_bundle Packaged selection
sepsis3 Every qualifying ICU stay
first_sepsis3 First-ever ICU stay, if it qualifies
sepsis3_admission Suspicion within ±1 day of ICU admission
first_sepsis3_admission Both restrictions

The assistant only assembles calls; the definitions themselves are the packaged SQL described in vignette("sepsis-cohort-definitions").

Non-interactive use

With interactive = FALSE the assistant returns the plan immediately. Values you leave out take the documented defaults (MIMIC-IV demo, SCI cohort, patient scope), so a non-interactive call is a reproducible way to generate a standard script. An invalid explicit combination fails during planning instead of being silently widened.
